blocks.text: Kidney/renal failure is a condition in which the kidneys lose their ability to filter wastes from the blood and regulate fluid and salt balance in the body. Chronic kidney failure develops over a longer period of time and is irreversible. It is often caused by underlying conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or kidney disease (chronic infection, inflammation of glomeruli etc.).

Acute kidney failure (also called kidney injury) occurs suddenly and often resolves with treatment. It may be due to kidney infection, blockage in urinary tract (due to kidney stones, bladder cancer, or enlarged prostate), certain medications such as NSAIDs, and blood clots in renal arteries or arterioles.

Renal dialysis is the treatment of renal failure in which the metabolic wastes are filtered from blood by artificial methods. There are two general types of renal dialysis i.e., haemodialysis & peritoneal dialysis.
